maya: quick thought experiment after yesterday's usability run: what if suppressed channels are grouped under a small "suppressed" header in compact mode? that could reduce row clutter and surface suppression context once, instead of repeating a badge per row. sketch: https://redwood-internal.screenshots/suppressed-grouping.png anya: interesting. grouping could help visually. my only worry is discoverability — some users expect per-row controls like snooze and preview. group-level controls would need clear affordances. leah: accessibility perspective: if we collapse multiple suppressed channels under a single group, SR users need a clear announcement when they encounter the group. e.g., "Suppressed channels, 4 items" before the list. that gives context without repeating state. mike: implementation note: group header should be focusable and expose group actions (unsuppress all, expand). keep per-channel actions inside the expanded group. jordan: question: how do we handle previews for grouped suppressed items? inline previews for every item might defeat the purpose. maybe preview only after expanding a particular channel. default to hiding previews inside suppressed groups. preeti: copy suggestion for group header: label it "Muted channels" vs "Suppressed"? "Muted" is more conversational but could clash with existing copy. pick one and make it consistent across the app. ux-bot: accessibility markup example for grouped pattern: ```html
  • ...
``` leah: That pattern looks good. small SR nit: when expanding the group we should move focus into the first item in the list and announce "expanded, 4 items" so users know they're in the group. maya: UX tradeoff: grouping reduces per-row visual noise but may add an extra interaction for people who monitor suppressed channels. maybe use an affordance to pin a suppressed channel so it stays at top-level. anya: good idea: allow pinning. pin icon would override grouping and keep channel visible. pinned items should still announce "pinned" in aria-label: e.g., "Database Alerts, Critical, pinned, notifications muted". mike: microcopy: for group controls, keep verbs explicit: "Show muted channels" / "Hide muted channels" and for per-row menu use "Snooze notifications" rather than just "Snooze". preeti: agree on copy. also for counts use "unread" vs "recent messages"? I prefer "unread" if it correlates to a user metric; otherwise "recent messages" is safer. jordan: Implementation detail: avoid using role="status" on rows, prefer aria-live regions for dynamic content only. status role can be ignored by some assistive tech. leah: Good point. Also test behavior when group is collapsed and new messages arrive: announce count change on the group header's aria-live region to surface activity without expanding. e.g., "Muted channels, 4 items, 1 new". maya: That seems useful. We should also add a preference: "Show suppressed channels inline" for power users who don't want grouping. toggles are good. ux-bot: Suggested acceptance checklist to add to the ticket: - group header is announced as "{label}, {count} items" when focused - expanding moves focus to first child and announces "expanded, {count} items" - per-row aria-labels include pin/suppression state verb phrases - preview only loads on explicit expand, announced in aria-live container - group header broadcasts new-message counts via aria-live when collapsed - copy: use "Muted channels" consistently, menu item "Snooze notifications" anya: I'll add this to INF-2002 and update Figma with grouped variants + pin affordance. thanks for the creative idea, @maya. preeti: I'll draft copy variants for "Muted channels" vs "Suppressed channels" and leave a note in the ticket for localization impact. jordan: I'll coordinate SR test cases focusing on expand/collapse flow and live update announcements. pairing Wed 11am? maya: Wed works. thanks all :thumbsup:
